dedupe_keys.name: nist community resilience planning guide indicator inventory and tracr county resilience data

description: The NIST community resilience programme publishes a set of products for planning the resilience of buildings and infrastructure systems. The Community Resilience Planning Guide, in two volumes, sets out a six-step process for communities to plan for hazards and recover, and is supported by Guide Briefs, a Playbook and planning templates. The Community Resilience Indicator Inventory compiles 56 resilience assessment frameworks with 3,298 indicators and 7,165 measures, and the Tracking Community Resilience (TraCR) database holds data for all 3,230 counties or county equivalents in the contiguous United States, Hawaii, Alaska, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands. The page also lists the Alternatives for Resilient Communities (ARC) tool. Access to the products is free online as NIST publications and data; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: the Guide is a planning method and document, and the indicators and TraCR measures are drawn from other sources, so their definitions and years vary. Coverage is the United States. It supports resilience and emergency planning across power, water, transport, communication and building systems, and selection of indicators for resilience models; related records are the NIST ARC tool and IN-CORE.
